properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 5:38AM MDT until September 30 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Southwest New Mexico including Dona Ana, Otero, Luna,
Sierra, Grant, and Hidalgo Counties. Far West Texas, including El
Paso and Hudspeth Counties.

* WHEN...Through 6AM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical moisture will be transported northward ahead of decaying
Tropical Cyclone Polo today, bringing widespread showers and
thunderstorms to the region. High rainfall rates and repeated
rounds of rain up to 4 inches may result in instances of flash
flooding. Heavy rainfall from last week has saturated soils and
will elevate the flood threat further into Wednesday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 29 at 2:54AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
The combination of hot temperatures and elevated humidity levels
will produce heat index values between 108 and 111 degrees for
several hours this afternoon into this evening. A few locations
may briefly experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

If you plan to spend time outside, drink plenty of water, wear
light weight and light colored clothing and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 1:18AM CDT until October 2 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Texas, including the following
counties, Brown, Callahan, Coke, Coleman, Concho, Crockett, Fisher,
Haskell, Irion, Jones, Kimble, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Nolan,
Runnels, San Saba, Schleicher, Shackelford, Sterling, Sutton,
Taylor, Throckmorton and Tom Green.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There is an increased danger to lives and property due to flash
flooding. Flash flooding is likely and considerable flash
flooding is possible.

- Multiple rounds of heavy rain are possible through Thursday night
as an influx of moisture arrives from the remnants of a tropical
disturbance. This will coincide with an approaching upper level
low pressure system and an associated frontal boundary. High
precipitable water values will support efficient rainfall
production with this activity. Model guidance suggests heavy rain
and thunderstorms capable of producing rainfall totals in the 2
to 4 inch range across the watch area. Locally higher amounts of
7+ inches can occur.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Fisher; Nolan; Sterling; Coke; Runnels; Irion; Tom Green; Concho; Crockett; Schleicher; Sutton; Haskell; Throckmorton; Jones; Shackelford; Taylor; Callahan; Coleman; Brown; McCulloch; San Saba; Menard; Kimble; Mason
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 28 at 10:54AM CDT by NWS San Angelo TX
properties.description:
The threat for very heavy rainfall and significant flash flooding is
increasing across west central Texas mainly Tuesday night through
Thursday. The combination of the remnants of Hurricane Polo from the
Pacific, abundant tropical moisture and a cold front will result in
periods of very heavy rainfall which may produce localized
significant flash flooding. Looks like the heaviest rainfall will
set up mainly east of a Sweetwater to Ozona line with widespread
2 to 3 inches. Isolated totals of around 10 inches are not out of
the question by Thursday evening mainly east of a Coleman to
Sonora line. Please keep up with the latest weather information
including watches and warnings.
